title: String Matching in an Array
statement: You get a list `words` of distinct strings. Find each word that occurs as a contiguous piece (a substring) inside at least one other word of the list, and return all such words in a list, each listed once. The result may be in any order; return an empty list when no word qualifies.
constraints: words[i] contains only lowercase English letters
All strings in words are distinct
notes:
## Intuition

A word belongs in the answer when some other word contains it. With at most 100 words of at most 30 letters, simply asking every ordered pair "does `words[j]` contain `words[i]`?" is fast, and a built-in substring search answers each question. Listing every substring of every word into a set would also work, but it does far more work than needed.

## Approach

1. Start with an empty `result`.
2. For each word `words[i]`, scan every other word `words[j]` (skip `j === i`, since a word always contains itself).
3. If `words[j].includes(words[i])`, add `words[i]` to `result` and `break`: one container is enough, and stopping keeps each word from being added twice.
4. Return `result`.

## Example 1, step by step

`words = ["mass", "as", "hero", "superhero"]`.

- `i = 0`, `"mass"`: no other word contains it.
- `i = 1`, `"as"`: `"mass"` contains it, so `result = ["as"]`.
- `i = 2`, `"hero"`: `"mass"` and `"as"` do not, `"superhero"` does, so `result = ["as", "hero"]`.
- `i = 3`, `"superhero"`: nothing else is long enough to hold it.

The answer is `["as", "hero"]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n² · L²) in the worst case for n words of length up to L, since each of the n² pair checks may scan up to L² characters (usually far fewer).
- Space: O(n) for the result list.

## Pitfalls

- Comparing a word with itself would put every word in the answer; skip `i === j`.
- Without the `break`, a word contained in two other words would be listed twice.
- The relation is not symmetric: test whether the other word contains this one, not the reverse.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `result` | words found inside some other word |
| `i` | index of the word being tested |
| `j` | index of the possible containing word |
